clue.text: Order DUKW originally for amphibious troops

parts.note: to order is to command
the amphibious lorry DUKW is called a duck, and duck is a cricket score of nothing, the letter O

explanation.surface: A wartime instruction that the first landing craft be sent for marines.
explanation.walkthrough: DUKW was the original spelling of the Second World War amphibious truck everyone called a 'duck'; a duck in cricket is a score of nought, written O.
explanation.definitionFit: Commandos are raiding forces, often landed from the sea in combined operations.

clue.text: Capsize vessel, going under in full view

indicators.note: in a down clue the vessel sits beneath the other piece

parts.note: openly visible means overt
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A boat tips over and sinks in front of everyone watching.
explanation.definitionFit: To capsize is to turn upside down, as boats do.

clue.text: Perhaps scorn married man who cuts a folksy figure

definitions.text: man who cuts a folksy figure

indicators.note: suggests the letters of the following words might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Someone may sneer at a husband who has taken up a quaint rustic pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges the twelve letters of SCORN and MARRIED. Morris dancing is a traditional English folk dance done with bells, sticks and handkerchiefs.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional folk dancer performs figures, set dance patterns, in costume.

clue.text: He barely appears in the new arts unit

indicators.note: signals that the letters of the following words are made into something new

explanation.surface: A man turns up scantily dressed in a recently created university department.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist goes about without clothes, so he is seen bare.

clue.text: Not prepared to side with worker

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: Someone is unready to support a labourer in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: An unrehearsed remark is made casually, without preparation.

clue.text: A bit of Utopia — or is that a sign of the past?

indicators.note: says only a small run of letters is taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A philosopher wonders whether a fragment of a perfect society is a relic of history.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the last letter of Utopia and carries through 'or is' into the T of 'that'.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorist is a Greek verb tense marking simple past action.

clue.text: Saintly man — and a luminary

explanation.surface: A holy person who is also a shining light.
explanation.walkthrough: St Elmo is the patron saint of sailors; St Elmo's fire is the glow seen on masts in storms.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Elmo is a named saint, and his name labels a glowing electrical discharge, a source of light.

clue.text: Steps taken by feathered bird

parts.note: bird is slang for a young woman; here she dances wielding large plumed fans

explanation.surface: Footprints left by a fowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret routine where a dancer conceals herself behind big ostrich-plume fans.

clue.text: Cultivate a girl first, using some craft

indicators.note: the girl's name is put before the rest

parts.note: Flo is a short girl's name
to till is to cultivate soil

explanation.surface: Advice to court a young woman before doing anything with cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like guile, but it means boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fleet of boats or ships, craft being vessels.

clue.text: King Edward

explanation.surface: A royal named Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic monarch; Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic monarch, and the Victorian writer of limericks Edward of that surname.

clue.text: Uncouth fellow needs cutting down to size

definitions.text: Uncouth fellow needs cutting down to size

parts.words: Uncouth fellow needs cutting down to size
parts.note: reads as a lout to be humbled, but also an uncut gem awaiting the jeweller

explanation.surface: A boor who ought to be taken down a peg.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a good-hearted person lacking polish, from an unworked gemstone.

clue.text: The war god with horse and hound is something of a hawk

parts.note: Mars is the Roman god of war
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
a harrier is a hound used for hunting hares

explanation.surface: A warrior deity with steed and dog is rather aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' suggests a militarist, fitting the war god, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey of the wetlands, related to the hawks.

clue.text: When mixing emulsion, see it doesn't get on foodstuffs

indicators.note: the letters of the paint word are stirred up, less those of the small word

explanation.surface: A decorator warns that paint being stirred must not splash the groceries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see it doesn't get on' tells you to take ON out of EMULSION; 'mixing' rearranges the remaining EMULSI.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakfast cereal mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit, counted among foods.

clue.text: Coloured, like Hazel

parts.note: Hazel looks like a woman's name but is the tree whose fruit has a familiar shade

explanation.surface: A girl called Hazel has a tan.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm mid-brown shade, the colour of a ripe hazel's fruit.

clue.text: Walking pace for this passage as well as mountain climbing

parts.note: and means as well as

indicators.note: going upward reads the volcano backwards

parts.note: Etna is the Sicilian volcano

explanation.surface: Hikers keep a slow pace through a gorge and on up the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking meaning at a moderate, walking speed.

clue.text: Social activity for those going rapidly downhill

definitions.text: Social activity for those going rapidly downhill

parts.words: Social activity for those going rapidly downhill
parts.note: sounds like a pastime for people in decline, but means skiers relaxing after the slopes

explanation.surface: Entertainment for people whose lives are falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening drinking and socialising at a resort after a day on the slopes.

clue.text: Agent with opening for Judas

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
a hole is an opening

explanation.surface: A double agent finds a chance to betray, like Judas.
explanation.walkthrough: Judas looks like the traitor, but a judas is a peephole in a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A judas is a small peephole in a door, letting someone look out unseen.

clue.text: Bear repeated ridicule

indicators.note: says the bear's name is written out twice in a row

parts.note: Pooh is A. A. Milne's teddy bear

explanation.surface: A teddy keeps on being mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss scornfully is to scoff or deride.

clue.text: Docile and a perhaps indifferent people lived here

indicators.note: signals that the letters of the gentle word might be reordered

parts.note: the setter meant the letters of docile plus two As; as printed 'and' would add N and D

explanation.surface: A meek, apathetic population once lived somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Laodicea was the ancient city whose church Revelation calls lukewarm. As printed the fodder cannot give the answer: the setter meant DOCILE with two As, and 'and' adds letters the answer lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelation rebukes the church in this ancient Phrygian city for being lukewarm, neither hot nor cold.

clue.text: Take sweetheart to wife

parts.note: the heart, or middle letter, of the word sweet
a wife is a spouse

explanation.surface: A man marries his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one marriage, but 'Take' alone is the definition, as in taking up a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt or support a cause or belief, embracing it.

clue.text: Protective coloration for relief workers

parts.note: sounds like camouflage in nature, but means a scarlet emblem guarding humanitarian staff

explanation.surface: Camouflage worn by aid staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The humanitarian movement whose scarlet emblem on white protects medics in war.

clue.text: Soldiers told off for bloomer

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold

explanation.surface: Troops are reprimanded for a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake, fitting the scolding, but it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: An exotic flowering plant, a bloomer being anything that flowers.

clue.text: Religious music I love is not on the loud speaker

indicators.note: says these letters are not present in the piece of music

parts.note: an oratorio is a large-scale sacred choral work
love is a zero score in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A churchgoer complains that sacred choral music he enjoys is missing from the PA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loud speaker' poses as a PA system, but it is a person speaking out.
explanation.definitionFit: A public speaker who addresses audiences forcefully.

clue.text: Proper 'search made for tenant farmer in Us

indicators.note: signals the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A thorough investigation is launched for an American smallholder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'search is research with its first syllable clipped; together with PROPER its letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In the American South, a tenant who works land for a share of the crop.

clue.text: One spot, filled with new red pimples

indicators.note: the first piece has the second placed inside it

parts.note: an ace is the playing card with a single pip

explanation.surface: A single blemish swells with fresh angry spots.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin condition producing inflamed spots, especially in teenagers.

clue.text: Pine prickle

explanation.surface: A conifer's needle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the tree but means to long for.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something, and a tingling irritation of the skin.

clue.text: Study of movement of cattle with the twitches

parts.note: kine is an old plural of cow
tics are involuntary twitches

explanation.surface: A farm researcher observes how restless herds move.
explanation.definitionFit: The branch of mechanics dealing with motion and the forces causing it.

clue.text: See at last, the true light

indicators.note: takes only the final letter of the word before

parts.note: real means true

explanation.surface: A mystic finally glimpses the genuine illumination.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate and airy, weightless as if not of this world.
